candidates.story: NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform: OpenShell and Sentry
candidates.reason: The exact-timestamped announcement is inside the 24-hour priority window. A versioned OpenShell release, detailed support matrix and independent context support a consequential, non-duplicate deployment analysis that separates software available for evaluation from a hardware-backed reference design whose standalone availability was not established.

candidates.story: Cloudflare cf agentic CLI open beta
candidates.reason: The event is fresh, but independent context was too limited for a source-diverse long-form article in this run, and the NVIDIA release offered a stronger operator decision.

The development materially overlaps existing legacy Kitesurf coverage. That article lacks an automated newsroom provenance record, so an automated update is not permitted, while a separate article would duplicate the topic.
Only a calendar date could be established, so the story could not clear the exact-time freshness gate. This was also the strongest rejected lead in the immediately preceding skipped run.
The AI material was high-level and did not support a distinct, consequential 1,200-word operational article.

decision.reason: NVIDIA's announcement is fresh, consequential and not already covered. The article gives operators a bounded deployment decision: OpenShell v0.1.2 is released software that can be inspected and tested now, while Sentry is presently evidenced as a BlueField-4 and DOCA reference design rather than a separately verified generally available product.

claims.text: NVIDIA announced the Open Agent Safety Platform at 09:00 UTC on 28 September 2026, inside the priority window.
The platform pairs a software runtime with a hardware-backed reference design.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 platform and product descriptions; availability categories remain separate.

claims.text: OpenShell v0.1.2 was the latest stable release checked and was published at 03:58 UTC on 28 September 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 GitHub release metadata at retrieval time; latest status must be rechecked before approval.

claims.text: The v0.1.2 release includes packaged CLI, gateway, prover, sandbox and supervisor artefacts.
NVIDIA labels the stable OpenShell track for production use within the documented support matrix.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 release-level table and production-scope language.

claims.text: The support matrix covers Linux amd64 and arm64 plus Apple-silicon macOS with Docker Desktop, while Windows WSL2 is experimental.
Linux enforcement depends on documented runtime and kernel facilities including Landlock and seccomp.
OpenShell separates gateway, supervisor and sandbox responsibilities.
NVIDIA says the supervisor can apply controls to HTTP, GraphQL and MCP traffic.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 network-control description; not treated as independent validation.

claims.text: NVIDIA says credential substitution is designed to keep secrets outside the workload.
Agent-proposed policy changes remain pending for human review by default and self-approval is barred.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 policy proposal and approval workflow.

claims.text: The policy prover checks permissions represented in its model rather than proving every runtime behaviour.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 policy prover scope plus bounded editorial interpretation.

claims.text: NVIDIA says Sentry uses BlueField-4 and DOCA and can quarantine suspicious actions in milliseconds.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 Sentry description; performance language remains explicitly attributed.

claims.text: The checked NVIDIA availability material did not establish a standalone Sentry release or release date.
claims.sourceLocator: Bounded finding from the announcement availability section and linked OpenShell materials.

claims.text: CNBC reports that reference-design partners are intended to bring products to market.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 partner and market context; not proof of current product availability.

claims.text: WIRED independently describes OpenShell as generally released and Sentry as the BlueField layer while noting uncertain adoption.
Teams can evaluate OpenShell now but should assess Sentry as a separate procurement and integration path.
claims.sourceLocator: Operational synthesis from release, support, availability and market evidence.

claims.text: Index Us did not install, benchmark or penetration-test OpenShell or Sentry.
claims.sourceLocator: Reporting-method disclosure: all retained evidence consists of public documentation, release metadata and reporting rather than an Index Us product test.
